newsitem.title: CHINA: France's Chirac urges more firms to come to China.
newsitem.headline: France's Chirac urges more firms to come to China.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac on Saturday opened a major French hi-tech exhibition in China's largest city and urged more French firms to set up shop in China, saying the country was too important to ignore.

"Everyone can see the scope and pace of the transformations that make China, now, and even more so in the future, one of the very greatest of world powers," Chirac said in a speech to open the five-day exhibition.
"French companies are aware of this. They are already present," he said. "They must be more present."

Chirac arrived in Shanghai shortly before midday after a three-day visit to Beijing which included the signing of a communique on increased bilateral cooperation and $1.8 billion in new contracts for French firms.

Chirac said it was encouraging that three-quarters of the 300 firms at the Shanghai exhibition were small or medium-sized and were new to the China market. He pledged to lend government support to boosting French exports to the country.
After his opening address, Chirac toured the exhibition, stopping to shake hands, wave or greet executives from participating companies.
"He told us he hopes we can get more projects in China," said Wang Honglu, area export manager for CSEE Transport, which has sold signalling systems to China's railways.
The participating companies include energy, transportation, aviation, construction, infrastructure and telecommunications firms.

"For all of the exhibitions we have done in the world, this is one of the most important," said Chiche Portiche, exhibition manager for the government-backed Agency for the International Promotion of French Technology and Trade.
"We find in two or three years' time the effect of such an exhibition is multiplied by five," Portiche said.
Chirac earlier had lunch with Shanghai's mayor Xu Kuangdi. He is scheduled to leave for Paris on Sunday.
